places.ad: Coney Island, Punggol, Singapore (West entrance off Punggol Promenade / East entrance off Pasir Ris side; to confirm at geocode)
places.w: A 133-hectare island off Punggol, once owned by the Aw brothers of Tiger Balm. In 1950 it was sold to a businessman who planned a resort modelled on New York's Coney Island. Since October 2015 a 50-hectare NParks park has kept it deliberately rustic: casuarina woods, a 2.5 km car-free trail, hidden beaches and bridges at both ends to the mainland.

places.ad: Punggol Point foreshore (Punggol Point Park), Punggol, Singapore
places.w: A National Heritage Board historic site. On 23 February 1942, during the Japanese Sook Ching operation, a Hojo Kempei firing squad killed some 300–400 Chinese civilians on the Punggol foreshore. Human remains turned up in the sand in 1977 and 1997. An NHB marker set up in 1995, for the 50th anniversary of the end of WWII, records the killings.

places.ad: Punggol Point Road, Punggol, Singapore
places.w: A seafront park at the northern tip of Punggol, opened on 20 November 2011 at the old Punggol Point fishing-village beach. People come for the sunset over the Strait of Johor, the jetty views across to Malaysia, and the WWII Sook Ching memorial on its foreshore.

places.ad: Waterway Point, beside Punggol MRT/Punggol Waterway, Punggol, Singapore (street + postal to confirm at geocode)
places.w: Punggol's main mall, with more than 200 stores, on the banks of Punggol Waterway next to the MRT. It is the town's main food cluster, covered in its own Eatbook food guide, and the jumping-off point for the waterway park.

places.ad: 78 Punggol Walk, Singapore
places.w: One of Singapore's oldest houses: a 1902 single-storey tropical bungalow built for Alexander Cashin and named for his mother Josephine Matilda — the Cashins being the Eurasian family whose patriarch became Singapore's first Eurasian millionaire. Conserved by URA in Feb 2000 and restored (façade and interior) as the clubhouse of the 'A Treasure Trove' condominium in 2015; view from Punggol Walk.
places.k: Conserved 1902 bungalow; condo clubhouse — exterior view only

places.ad: Punggol Waterway (Sentul Crescent / Punggol Central), Punggol, Singapore
places.w: The 4.2-km park along Singapore's longest man-made waterway, in four themed zones (Nature Cove, Recreation Zone, Heritage Zone on Old Punggol Road, Green Gallery) linked by five photogenic bridges — the dome-shaped Jewel Bridge for sunsets over the Punggol and Serangoon reservoirs, the snaking red Sunrise Bridge at the eastern Sunrise Gateway, plus the Wave, Adventure and Kelong bridges. Otters are regulars.
places.k: Free; best at sunrise (east) and sunset (Jewel Bridge, west)

places.ad: One Punggol, 1 Punggol Drive, #01-12, Singapore 828629
places.w: NLB's five-storey regional library in the One Punggol hub (opened in stages Jan-Apr 2023), built as an inclusive library with interactive exhibits, tech zones and a free MakeIT maker space for 3D printing, digital cutting and robotics.

places.ad: 30 Punggol Field, Singapore 828812
places.w: Punggol's only mosque (2015, capacity 4,000), designed by Formwerkz Architects as an 'open mosque': a porous, naturally ventilated village cluster of prayer hall, school and offices around landscaped courts — widely published as a model of contemporary Singapore mosque architecture.
places.k: Visitors welcome outside prayer times; dress modestly

places.ad: Punggol Coast, Punggol Way, Singapore (beside Punggol Coast MRT)
places.w: Singapore's first 'enterprise district' (~50 ha, phase 1 opened from Q3 2024), marketed as Singapore's "Silicon Valley" and built around the Singapore Institute of Technology's new Punggol campus (classes from Sept 2024); the BCA Green Mark Platinum campus runs on 20,000+ sensors and smart lamp-posts. Campus Heart houses the SIT Visitor Gallery.
places.k: SIT Visitor Gallery; pair with Punggol Coast Hawker Centre

places.ad: Punggol Point Park, end of Punggol Point Road, Punggol, Singapore
places.w: A long-standing, iconic jetty at Punggol Point — the coast of kelongs such as the 1969 Sea Palace kelong restaurant-cum-nightclub on stilts that made Punggol Point a seafood-and-leisure destination; NHB names Punggol Jetty among Punggol's heritage landmarks. Views to Pulau Ubin and the Johor Strait.
places.k: Free; sunset; combine with Punggol Point Park

places.ad: 681 Punggol Drive, Singapore 820681
places.w: HDB's new-generation neighbourhood centre on the Punggol Waterway (opened 2018–19), designed by Serie Architects with Multiply Architects as a stepped garden of terraces cascading to the water, with a rooftop community garden and polyclinic — published internationally by Dezeen and designboom. Houses Lao Jiang Superior Soup and Rise & Grind.
places.k: Free; climb the terraces to the rooftop garden for waterway views

places.ad: Tebing Lane / 50 Punggol East, beside Punggol Promenade Riverside Walk, Singapore
places.w: An Artbox-style cluster of shipping-container eateries, a roller-skating rink and plant nurseries next to the Social Innovation Park, where the Riverside Walk meets Tebing Lane's cafés — the casual evening hangout of Punggol East (Daniel Food Diary, TheSmartLocal, Little Day Out, Sassy Mama).
places.k: Evenings; Riviera LRT exit A, then walk to the riverside

places.ad: Punggol Road / Punggol Drive / Punggol Place, Punggol, Singapore
places.w: HDB's first eco-precinct (2010): seven 16-storey blocks with rainwater harvesting, solar-powered common areas, a wind-channelling 'eco-deck' and a community garden — the first public-housing project to win the Green Mark Platinum award, and the pilot for the Punggol eco-town.
places.k: Residential estate — view from Punggol Drive; the eco-deck and garden are for residents

places.ad: Punggol Walk / Punggol Way / Sumang Link, along Punggol Waterway, Singapore
places.w: Singapore's first waterfront public housing, won in an international HDB design competition by Group8asia with Aedas: stepped blocks that echo Asian rice terraces, sky terraces and roof gardens cascading down to the waterway (Waterway Terraces II is Green Mark Platinum) — published by designboom and awarded at the RTF Sustainability Awards 2016.
places.k: Best seen from the Punggol Waterway promenade near Sumang

places.ad: 6 Tebing Lane #01-04, Punggol, Singapore 828835
places.w: Singapore's round-the-clock prawning pond by the Punggol riverside: six ponds under a thatched, lantern-hung roof, rods and bait included, barbecue pits and salt to grill your catch on the spot, and a cheap beer garden — Time Out's Punggol pick, also in TheSmartLocal's and Honeycombers' prawning guides.
places.k: Open 24 hours; from $20/hour; grill and beer on site

places.n: Kwang Kee Teochew Fish Porridge (One Punggol)
places.ad: One Punggol Hawker Centre, #02-19, Punggol, Singapore (street + postal to confirm at geocode)
places.w: Punggol branch of a Teochew fish-porridge stall founded in 1962 and on the MICHELIN Bib Gourmand list every year since 2021. Known for a light, clean, sweet-savoury broth and fresh fish slices; the original is at Newton Food Centre.

places.ad: One Punggol Hawker Centre, #02-14, Punggol, Singapore (street + postal to confirm at geocode)
places.w: Silky Cantonese congee in more than 10 versions. The signature mixed porridge comes loaded with century egg, chicken, pork liver, cuttlefish, meatball and fried you tiao. This is the second stall, after Our Tampines Hub.

places.ad: One Punggol Hawker Centre, #02-11, Punggol, Singapore (street + postal to confirm at geocode)
places.w: Penang-style rojak from a Malaysian family recipe: tropical fruit, crunchy vegetables and fried dough fritters tossed in a thick sweet-spicy paste. It moved here from Joo Chiat Place when One Punggol opened.

places.ad: One Punggol Hawker Centre, #02-28, Punggol, Singapore (street + postal to confirm at geocode)
places.w: One Punggol's bak chor mee specialist: springy noodles tossed in vinegar-chilli with minced pork, plus a seafood-abalone version — picked by both Seth Lui and Her World in their One Punggol Hawker Centre top-10s.

places.ad: 500 New Punggol Road, #02-05, The Punggol Settlement, Singapore 828617
places.w: A no-frills izakaya hidden on the second storey of The Punggol Settlement, where Japanese bar grub comes with a waterfront sunset — a fixture on Punggol food guides from Lady Iron Chef (2018) to Eatbook's current 30-best list.

places.ad: 10 Tebing Lane, Singapore 828836
places.w: The Punggol waterfront café that set the template for the estate's brunch scene: all-day breakfast plates (eggs Benedict, bacon-and-egg waffles) in a house by Tebing Lane — named across Lady Iron Chef, Honeycombers and Eatbook's Punggol guides.

places.ad: 3 Punggol Point Road, The Punggol Settlement, Singapore 828694
places.w: The famous Sembawang white bee hoon — silky rice vermicelli soaked in a rich seafood broth with prawns, squid and egg — at its waterfront Punggol Settlement outlet, known for queues an hour long (Eatbook; Lady Iron Chef).

places.ad: Waterway Point (top floor), 83 Punggol Central, Singapore (unit to confirm at geocode)
places.w: Straightforward, meaty Western plates — ribeye, flame-grilled chicken — on Waterway Point's top floor; on both Lady Iron Chef's and Eatbook's Punggol food lists.

places.ad: One Punggol Hawker Centre, #02-34, 1 Punggol Drive, Singapore 828629
places.w: The beloved wing stall's sixth outlet: wings marinated through, coated in a light, crunchy batter and fried super-crisp and juicy, about $1.70 each — the One Punggol stall that Seth Lui, Her World, Daniel Food Diary and Mothership all name.

places.ad: One Punggol Hawker Centre, 1 Punggol Drive, Singapore 828629 (unit to confirm)
places.w: A steamed-food stall run by a hawker who spent years in the kitchens of the Ah Yat restaurant group — first on Eatbook's 11 best One Punggol stalls, and in Mothership's opening line-up.

places.n: Zi Jia Yong Tau Foo (One Punggol)
places.ad: One Punggol Hawker Centre, 1 Punggol Drive, Singapore 828629 (unit to confirm)
places.w: House-made yong tau foo — vegetables, ngoh hiang, fish cake — boiled or deep-fried to order, with nine noodle options from mee sua to claypot noodles (Eatbook's One Punggol 11; Mothership's opening list).

places.ad: #02-11/12 Northshore Plaza II, 418 Northshore Drive, Singapore
places.w: A work-friendly café on the Punggol waterfront serving Japanese rice bowls and sandos — reviewed by Eatbook and picked in Women's Weekly's new Sengkang & Punggol dining spots.

places.ad: The Punggol Settlement, 3 Punggol Point Road, Singapore 828694 (unit to confirm)
places.w: A Balinese-themed bar on the Punggol Settlement waterfront — grilled meats, bar bites and its golden buffalo wings with a sea breeze — on Lady Iron Chef's Punggol guide and Eatbook's current 30-best Punggol list.

places.ad: One Punggol Hawker Centre, 1 Punggol Drive, Singapore 828629 (unit to confirm)
places.w: Indonesian smashed fried chicken with fiery sambal — a One Punggol stall on Eatbook's 30 best Punggol list and in Mothership's opening line-up.

places.ad: Punggol, Singapore (address to confirm at geocode)
places.w: A sourdough-centric bakery-café that turned one starter into loaves, toasties, soups, pastas and pizzas when it opened in Punggol in Oct 2022 — covered by Miss Tam Chiak, Daniel Food Diary, Seth Lui, HungryGoWhere and Time Out, and on Eatbook's 30 best Punggol list.

places.ad: SAFRA Punggol, Punggol, Singapore (address to confirm at geocode)
places.w: The famous Alexandra zi char family's Punggol outlet, serving bold Singaporean zi char in a nostalgic MRT-themed dining room (Daniel Food Diary, Jul 2025); on Eatbook's 30 best Punggol food places.

places.ad: 6 Tebing Lane, #01-03, Singapore 828835
places.w: A four-outlet zi char favourite best known for crab — the claypot crab bee hoon above all — at its Punggol waterfront outlet on Tebing Lane (Time Out); on Eatbook's 30 best Punggol food places.

places.ad: The Punggol Settlement, 3 Punggol Point Road, Singapore 828694
places.w: CLOSED 2 May 2024. The seafood restaurant that carried the old 'Ponggol' spelling and the memory of the kelong-era Punggol seafood strip — in business since 1965, famous for chilli crab, lala bee hoon and mee goreng (Honeycombers) — quietly shut after 55 years (Seth Lui). Kept, flagged, as part of Punggol's food history.

pv.ss: Seth Lui May 2024: shut 2 May 2024 after 55 years

places.ad: Edgefield Plains, Punggol, Singapore (coffeeshop + unit to confirm at geocode)
places.w: A coffeeshop Japanese stall whose owner spent nine years as head chef of a famous ION Orchard tonkatsu restaurant — donburi and Japanese curry at hawker prices (Daniel Food Diary); on Eatbook's 30 best Punggol list.

places.ad: Punggol, Singapore (coffeeshop + unit to confirm at geocode)
places.w: Comforting Cantonese porridge from a stall with more than 40 years' experience, open from 7am until just after lunch — in Time Out's Punggol guide and Eatbook's 30 best Punggol food places.

places.ad: Oasis Terraces, 681 Punggol Drive #01-42/43, Singapore 820681
places.w: A homegrown soup specialist since 2011: a sweet-savoury, light seafood broth loaded with prawns, fish maw, pork slices, abalone slices and beancurd-skin fish sticks, over rice, hor fun or you mian — with an addictive chilli and fresh lard. Featured by Eatbook (Punggol guide) and reviewed by Seth Lui.

places.ad: Oasis Terraces, 681 Punggol Drive #01-06, Singapore 820681
places.w: Punggol's go-to waterfront brunch cafe: Australian-inspired big brekkies, avo toast, soft fluffy pancakes and generous mains like the mushroom chicken chop — picked by Eatbook's Punggol guide and City Nomads' Sengkang–Punggol dining guide.

places.n: Sixth Floor Oyster Cake (Northshore Plaza) — CLOSED
places.ad: Northshore Plaza I, 407 Northshore Drive #02-41, Singapore
places.w: A Punggol home business (named for the owner's sixth-floor HDB flat) that grew into a Northshore Plaza kiosk frying ultra-crisp Fuzhou oyster cakes — two whole oysters, minced meat and shrimp — covered by Eatbook and Women's Weekly. CLOSED: both outlets shut permanently after 28 Sep 2025 (Seth Lui).

pv.ss: Seth Lui: both outlets shut permanently after 28 Sep 2025 (owner's Instagram announcement)

places.ad: One Punggol Hawker Centre, 1 Punggol Drive #02-08, Singapore 828629
places.w: Third-generation hawker Madam Fauziah Isnin stirs a secret 15-spice beef rendang in 15–20 kg batches, served as nasi rendang or with lontong kampung, alongside mee rebus, mee soto and Malay kueh — a family recipe line going back to her grandparents' 1940s pop-up. Picked by Women's Weekly and Seth Lui at One Punggol.

places.ad: Waterway Point West Wing #01-72/73, 83 Punggol Central, Singapore 828761
places.w: The viral Kamakura warabimochi specialist (snaking queues at its 2024 Holland Village debut) opened its first dine-in café here in Oct 2024, with café-only warabimochi drinks, a kuromitsu soft serve dusted with kinako and a warabimochi-and-hot-matcha set — covered by Time Out, Mothership and Eatbook.

places.ad: Happy Hawkers coffeeshop, 671 Edgefield Plains, Punggol, Singapore
places.w: A Sarawakian-run coffeeshop stall (opened Feb 2023) that is one of the few places in the north-east for springy, shallot-oil kolo mee and a proper Kuching laksa, plus Sibu kampua and braised-pork rice — reviewed by both Seth Lui and Eatbook.

places.ad: #01-05/06, 10 Tebing Lane, Punggol, Singapore 828836
places.w: The Tebing Lane riverside café for Western-Asian mash-ups — prawn-paste chicken in a Hong Kong bolo bun, mala mushroom pasta, chicken-chop laksa — on Daniel Food Diary's Punggol cafés list, Eatbook's 30 best Punggol places and reviewed by Seth Lui and Miss Tam Chiak.

places.ad: 50 Punggol East #01-K36, Punggol, Singapore 828826
places.w: The Korean container kitchen at the Punggol East container park by Tebing Lane — spicy beef bulgogi rice and jjajangmyeon eaten outdoors by the river; on Eatbook's 30 best Punggol places and TheSmartLocal's container-park guide.

places.ad: #01-01/02, The Punggol Settlement, Punggol Point Road, Singapore 828617 (street no. printed as 3 / 500 — resolve at helper)
places.w: The big crab restaurant at the Punggol Settlement, looking out over Punggol Point Jetty: live seafood cooked zi-char style, with its salted-egg and black-pepper crabs as the calling cards — picked in Time Out's, Honeycombers' and TheSmartLocal's Punggol guides.

places.ad: #02-22 Northshore Plaza I, 407 Northshore Drive, Punggol, Singapore
places.w: The nostalgic HDB-void-deck eatery (born at Suntec City, reviewed there by Seth Lui, Eatbook and Miss Tam Chiak) in its Punggol branch: braised-pork-rice toppings over QQ noodles and salted-egg chicken rice under letterbox walls and old-school tiles — listed in Eatbook's Northshore Plaza guide and Daniel Food Diary's Punggol cafés.

places.ad: #02-13 One Punggol Hawker Centre, 1 Punggol Drive, Singapore 828629
places.w: The fourth outlet of the 1947 Golden Mile glutinous-rice-ball institution (pushcart on Jalan Sultan, Golden Mile from 1975): hand-rolled tang yuan in its signature uncrushed-peanut soup — named in Eatbook's and HungryGoWhere's One Punggol guides (a further outlet now also trades at Punggol Coast, per Women's Weekly).

places.ad: Foodgle Hub coffeeshop, Punggol Walk (near Sumang LRT), Punggol, Singapore (block + unit to confirm at geocode)
places.w: A halal Malay-Indonesian stall residents call 'the best nasi padang in Punggol' — moved from Sumang Link to the Foodgle Hub by Sumang LRT; morning queues for $5 nasi sambal goreng, a golden mee soto and nasi rawon. Reviewed by Seth Lui ('like an addict, I kept going back') and on Have Halal Will Travel's best nasi sambal goreng list.

places.ad: 218 Sumang Walk #01-10, Punggol, Singapore 820218
places.w: Muslim-owned satay grill in the heart of Punggol, selling meaty charcoal skewers in sets ($24–69) from 3pm until sold out — covered by Seth Lui on opening and in Have Halal Will Travel's Ultimate Guide to Halal Satay.
